description: The migration runner (Go `core/upgrade.Migrator`) against a recording driver. Each scenario registers `migrations`, adds `drivers` in order and runs `steps` on one migrator with target `target`. A driver reports `version` until `set_version` succeeds; a `*_fail` field makes that driver call fail with that message (`set_version_fail_for` limits `set_version_fail` to that one version); `stores_version` makes it a version-storing driver, for which the runner writes and reads no version file. A migration with `fail` fails its Up with that message; `down` gives it a Down, `down_fail` a failing one. `backups` creates backup directories before the first step; `recorded_backups` (`{schema: {dir: pre-run version}}`) creates directories that also carry the pre-run version saved beside them, in `<backup dir>.version` (an empty file is a recorded empty version). `calls` is what the step did, in order: `<schema> backup|restore <backup dir name>`, `<schema> up|down <version>`, `<schema> set_version <version>`. `history` is cumulative; `versions` is each schema's version file (`""` when absent); `stored` is what each driver reports as its version after the step; `backups` lists each schema's backup directories by name after the step; `pre_run_versions` is, per schema, every `<backup dir>.version` file beside the backups (by directory name) and nothing else; `no_version_dir` lists schemas whose `<data dir>/<schema>` directory must not exist. `error` is the exact error text, or null. Each migration may also carry `verify` (a passing verify step) or `verify_fail`, and `cancel` cancels the run's context after its Up. A scenario may set `final_verify` or `final_verify_fail` (the migrator's final verify), `data_dir` (an explicit data dir instead of XDG), `registry: own` with `default_migrations` (registered in the default registry, which an own registry must not see) and `locked_backups` (old backups that cannot be removed). A step may set `canceled` (run with a canceled context). Calls also log `<schema> verify <version>` and `<schema> final_verify <version>`. A `set_version` call follows each migration that applied (after its `verify`), each `down` of a rollback (the version before that migration), and each restore (the version the run started at); an empty version logs as `<schema> set_version ` with nothing after the space. `events` lists what the run published, in order, under the default topics; `duration_ms` is left out of the payloads (runners check it is a non-negative integer where present). `warnings` lists, as prefixes, what the run logged. A scenario may set `baseline` (`{schema: {version, error}}`): the Migrator gets a baseline function that logs `<schema> baseline` and returns that schema's `version` (empty when omitted) or fails with its `error`; a schema without an entry returns empty; without the field there is no baseline function. The baseline call follows the stored-version read and precedes the pending selection, backup and every `up`; a non-empty result is recorded like any version and publishes `baselined` (`from` is empty, `to` the recorded version), and a failing function or record is the schema's error, prefixed `baseline: `. A driver with `lock` is a lockable driver (Go `Locker`, Rust `Locker` via `as_locker`): `Lock` logs `<schema> lock`, the returned unlock logs `<schema> unlock`, and a lockable driver also logs every `Version()` read as `<schema> version`, so the order is pinned (`Status` reads it too, and takes no lock). `lock_fail` makes `Lock` fail with that message (no unlock follows: nothing was acquired); `lock_blocked` makes it wait for the run's context, so it fails with the context's error and the step must set `canceled`; `lock_sets_version` makes the lock, once acquired, report that version from then on (what another process recorded while this one waited); `unlock_fail` makes the unlock fail. A lockable driver is locked before its version is read and unlocked after its run ends, after any rollback, on every path once the lock is held; a failed `Lock` is the schema's error prefixed `lock: `, and a failed unlock is logged as a warning prefixed `warning: unlock <schema>: ` and changes no result.
